Higiene never sends your location or your searches anywhere: distances and search run on this phone. (Android\'s own location service works as it does for any app.) The app downloads files from the FSA (ratings) and Ordnance Survey (postcodes). If switched on, it downloads a weekly OpenStreetMap file from this app\'s GitHub page and loads chain logos from Wikimedia or Facebook for the chains on your screen, so those services can see which chain is shown. Only if you add your own Google key or Mapillary token does the app ask Google or Mapillary about a business you open (its name, address or position); they also see your IP address. There are no accounts, adverts or analytics.

How to get a Google key
How to get a Mapillary token

1. Open console.cloud.google.com, create a project and add a billing account. Google asks for one even for free use.
2. In APIs & Services, enable Places API (New) and Street View Static API.
3. In Credentials, create an API key.
4. Restrict the key. Under API restrictions, choose the two APIs above. Under Application restrictions, choose Android apps and add this app with the package name and SHA-1 below.
5. Optional: in Quotas, set a daily limit as a backstop.
6. Paste the key above and tap Save and test.

Google\'s free allowance each month (shared by all your Google projects): 1,000 business look-ups and 10,000 street photos. Higiene stops at %1$d look-ups and %2$d photos a day, and %3$d and %4$d a month, so it stays inside the free allowance. Using Google is under Google\'s terms (maps.google.com/help/terms_maps).

1. Sign up or sign in at mapillary.com.
2. Open mapillary.com/dashboard/developers and register an app. It only needs to read.
3. Copy its Client Token (it starts with MLY|) and paste it above.
Mapillary is free. Its photos are used when there is no Google key or Google has no photo. They are by Mapillary contributors under CC BY-SA 4.0.
